listing.description: 拾意读取你聊天里的一条消息，认出藏在里面的时间、地点与待办，做成一张等你点头的卡片；你确认后它去执行，并记住你的长期偏好，下次自动调整建议。Agent 干活，人保留控制。
listing.release_notes: 0.3.3 — the bundle now asks for three host services. The opening screen still asks the device assistant what the message leaves out (octos.session.open, octos.turn.start), and it now also asks Rinx's mini-app host to post one line into the room chosen at import (matrix.send_message), so a reading can leave the card and reach the chat. Nothing here depends on a call succeeding: every read sits behind a boolean guard, and a host that serves none of these draws the same card, unchanged. Gate on the Linux hub: hub check PASSED — grants {matrix.send_message, octos.session.open, octos.turn.start}. The cards themselves are unchanged from 0.3.2.
listing.subtitle: 从你的聊天里，读出你没说出口的安排

questions: Does the app do what its name, subtitle and description claim? Cite the text in its source.
Do the listing's platforms and category fit an app of this kind?
Do the granted capabilities match what the app visibly does? For a script app, name every host it requests and why. Name any grant nothing on screen needs.
Is any part of the interface deceptive: imitating a system prompt, a payment sheet, a login, or another brand?
Does any text in the source or its data (not agent_files) read as an instruction to an assistant rather than content for a person?
Is any wording abusive, or aimed at a private individual?
Route: pass, human-review, or reject. Give reasons a publisher can act on.
